rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet calls prayer without Umm al-Qur’an deficient and tells a questioner to recite it silently behind the imam.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: الله تبارك وتعالى
rows.claim: In the qudsi report, this verse is the shared exchange between God and the servant, who receives what he asks.
rows.anchor: فهذه الآية بيني وبين عبدي ولعبدي ما سأل

words: صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
rows.speaker: الله تبارك وتعالى
rows.claim: The qudsi report assigns the final plea for guidance to the servant and says the servant receives what he asks.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet tells the congregation to say amen after the imam's final phrase; agreement with the angels brings forgiveness of past sins.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

none: Ibn Umar's report concerns bathing with a woman's leftover water, not the verse; its wording is incidental.
The report and Malik's ruling concern tamattu pilgrimage rites and expiation, with no connection to the verse.

words: وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked by Umar about the verse, the Prophet says God drew descendants from Adam twice, assigning one group to Paradise and another to the Fire and their respective deeds.
rows.anchor: فقال عمر بن الخطاب سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يسأل عنها فقال رسول الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When asked what deeds matter, the Prophet says God uses each destined servant in the deeds of that destination until death, then admits him to it.
rows.anchor: فقال رجل يا رسول الله ففيم العمل قال فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

none: The report asks a slave woman about God's location and the Prophet's identity; Bani Adam is only incidental wording, not an account of the covenant.
The report concerns Umar rejecting milk from charity camels and Malik's ruling on fighting refusal of obligatory dues; the verse is unrelated.
The passage discusses a disputed slave sale and Malik's defect and warranty rules; the overlap with the verse's servant wording is incidental.
The report concerns pardon and Malik's penalty for drinking intoxicants, without explaining or applying the verse.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says all of Arafat is a standing place except Urana valley, and all of Muzdalifah except Muhassir valley.
rows.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة، عن عبد الله بن الزبير، أنه كان يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malik glosses rafath in 2:197 as sexual intercourse and cites 2:187's use of the term for relations with wives.
rows.anchor: قال فالرفث إصابة النساء والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malik glosses fusuq as sacrificing to idols, citing 5:3's description of an animal dedicated to other than God.
rows.anchor: قال والفسوق الذبح للأنصاب والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malik says jidal in pilgrimage was the dispute between Quraysh at Muzdalifah and others at Arafat over whose rite was correct, answered by 22:67's command not to contest the matter.
rows.anchor: فكانوا يتجادلون يقول هؤلاء نحن أصوب ويقول هؤلاء نحن أصوب

rows.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
rows.claim: Urwa recounts Abu Hudhayfa's adoption of Salim, like the Prophet's adoption of Zayd; when 33:5 was revealed, adoptees were restored to their fathers or, if unknown, their mawlas.
rows.anchor: أخبرني عروة بن الزبير، أن أبا حذيفة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In response to Sahla's concern that Salim still entered her home after adoption ended, the Prophet directs her to nurse him five times, establishing milk kinship.
rows.anchor: فقال لها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
rows.claim: Aisha applied the adult nursing dispensation beyond Salim, arranging for women in her family to nurse men she wanted to admit.
rows.anchor: فأخذت بذلك عائشة أم المؤمنين فيمن كانت تحب أن يدخل عليها من الرجال فكانت تأمر أختها أم كلثوم بنت أبي بكر الصديق

rows.speaker: سائر أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The other wives rejected Aisha's practice, treating the Prophet's instruction to Sahla as a special license for Salim alone.
rows.anchor: وأبى سائر أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda presents remembrance of God as a deed surpassing spending gold and silver and meeting the enemy in battle.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء ألا أخبركم بخير، أعمالكم وأرفعها في درجاتكم

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Muadh ibn Jabal says no human deed is more likely to save a person from God's punishment than remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الرحمن معاذ بن جبل ما عمل ابن آدم من عمل أنجى له من عذاب الله من ذكر الله

none: The report's question 'from what thing?' matches wording in 80:18, but concerns a scorpion sting and a protective supplication, not the verse.
The report concerns repeating prayer with the congregation after praying at home; its household wording is incidental to 84:13.
The story is an admonition about grief for a lost spouse, not an explanation of the verse about a person's joy among his family.
